title: a-device-reaches-trouble-over-the-bus-never-by-import
intention: Any component raises a trouble through the base class it already inherits — an emission beside emit(), no import of the trouble device — and the trouble device drains those emissions into its held tickets and answers `live` and `clear` over the bus, so no device imports another device (db_domain stays the sole exception) and the isolation sieve reads green with the panel still live.
why: The trouble panel Akien opens shows live troubles because cairn/device.py and web_server/listener.py instantiate TroubleDevice directly — the panel works, and the isolation sieve reds both devices on every inspector run (2 live troubles, 3 findings, since the panel landed 2026-09-04). The lived symptom is a permanent red on the dashboard that nobody can clear without the code moving.
how: RATIFIED SHAPE (Akien 2026-09-07: 'a good choice. i'd forgotten it was it's own device!'): SENDING IS A TOOL, HOLDING IS OWNED. (a) DiagnosticBase (cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py, the mixin every BaseDevice composes) grows raise_trouble(identity, *, why, detail=None): it is emit() with the lane fixed — gate 'raise_trouble', one JSON file per emission under the raiser's own log home (~/.cairn/logs/<device>/<instance>/, the BreadcrumbLog shape). No import, no read-modify-write, import-light by the boot-order law. It pokes the lane through an INJECTED notifier (the set_diagnostic_receiver pattern — never an import in diagnostic.py) so a raise is live now, not on the next beat (memory shrinking-footprint-event-not-poll); with no notifier set, the beat drains. (b) TroubleDevice gets a shim (cairn/devices/trouble/shim.py — none exists today) that owns its subscription (memory device-owns-its-subscription): on the poke, and at-rest on the beat as the backstop, it drains raise_trouble emissions into CairnCommons/troubles/, damping by identity (count increments, truth never) in the ONE process that owns the store — two raisers of the same fault cannot race the JSON. TroubleDevice.raise_trouble stays as the drain's fold, not a public entry. (c) The shim answers `live` (JSON list) and `clear <identity> --by ... --what-changed ...` over the bus through the same contract inference_domain answers `infer` with (cairn/devices/codemother/watch.py:45 is the client pattern: connect_bus().request(device, verbs, ...)). Clearing is the recipient's alone — it stays behind the owner's gate. (d) cairn/device.py's _trouble_pane_data and web_server/listener.py's _handle_ws_troubles become bus requests for `live`. (e) The two raisers today — build_inspector's _file_troubles_for_new_findings (inspector.py:3181) and the tester's validation_store (:316) — stop instantiating TroubleDevice and raise through the base emission (the inspector is a machine under the cairn device; it raises through its holder). _reconcile_cleared_findings clears through the `clear` verb. The trouble-why rendering fix (idea fc075d9df7da: 'expected <about>; actual: <reason>') rides along at inspector.py:3194 since that line is rewritten here. (f) The probe cairn/devices/cairn/probes/trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles.py stops importing web_server.render: it asks web_server's `render` verb for the pane, or berths beside web_server if what it measures is web_server's rendering. OPEN, Akien's to settle if the default is wrong: the poke-vs-beat choice above defaults to poke (event not poll); the pure logging shape is beat-only and the panel then lags one beat.
falsifier: DONE when (1) `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector` reports zero device_isolation_holds findings; (2) `grep -rn 'cairn.devices.trouble' cairn --include=*.py` matches only under cairn/devices/trouble/ and the operator_inbox's read of live troubles (a tool reading the store, or a bus `live`); (3) a tools/base proof raises a trouble from a fixture device that imports nothing from cairn.devices and the emission lands in its log home; (4) trouble's proof shows two raises of one identity from two processes fold to ONE held ticket with count 2; (5) the probe trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles still proves green with a raised fixture trouble visible in the rendered pane within 1s of the raise (poke path) — the WebSocket push budget is measured, not assumed; (6) the two inspector troubles are cleared by reconcile through `clear`, not by hand. WRONG INTENT if the poke cannot be kept import-light — then the raise lands, the beat drains, and the panel's latency is one beat, stated in the charter.
traces_to: Law 6 — everything has exactly one owner and the owner alone gates writes: trouble's store is trouble's, and a direct TroubleDevice() from another device's process writes it ambiently. Ruling no-cross-device-imports (memory RULED; sieve 3f4887e): only db_domain may be imported across devices. Encapsulation is the complexity budget: each device stays inside CC's limit through the standard bus contract. Law 6's own test: 'anything called a tool that must gate writes at its own address is a machine' — the raise gates nothing (a tool, users not owners) and the hold gates the store (the trouble device). Law 7: a trouble is a diagnostic surface, loud; the raise is the same class as logging (Akien 2026-09-07).
